summary: Concrete non-duplicate MaterialDNA depth gap: closed-record validation is semantically fail-closed but not operationally bounded for malformed tables. validateKnownFields iterates every supplied key and appends one diagnostic per unknown field, embedding an unknown string key verbatim. A generated/persisted plain table with arbitrarily many unknown fields and/or very large string field names can therefore make rejected validation consume unbounded scan time and error-memory proportional to hostile input, conflicting with the MaterialDNA contract's bounded generation/persistence-work claim. Existing active repair-count PRs #313/#317 and the percent-key grammar finding do not address validator work/error budgets.
evidence: main src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau validateKnownFields uses pairs(record) over all supplied fields and appendError for every unknown key; unknown string keys are interpolated into diagnostics without a length cap.

validateRecipe traverses every declared nested record and accumulates all diagnostics in an errors array before returning; assertValidRecipe then table.concat's that full array. Dense history/anomaly arrays are capped, but malformed record cardinality and diagnostic count/bytes are not.

Docs/MATERIAL_DNA_CONTRACT.md explicitly characterizes validation/freezing as bounded content-generation/persistence work. The current closed-shape validator guarantees rejection semantics but does not bound work over rejected record shapes.

Repository search found no open/closed MaterialDNA validation-budget, diagnostic-budget, or field-cardinality repair. Active #313/#317 only bound maintenance.repairCount exactness; the existing key-grammar finding only removes '%' from project semantic values.

suggestedAcceptance: validation of malformed record shapes has a small explicit maximum diagnostic count and/or field-scan budget
unknown string field names are diagnostic-truncated or otherwise bounded without executing metamethods
ordinary valid recipes and existing exact diagnostics used by tests remain stable where practical
adversarial regressions prove very wide records and very long unknown field names fail closed with bounded error count/bytes
no schemaVersion, recipe identity, fixture content, or Studio behavior change
